tasks.gr12-genetics-inheritance-t2: Topic: Genetics and Inheritance. Cover genes, alleles, chromosomes, dominant and recessive inheritance, genotype, phenotype, homozygous and heterozygous conditions, monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, codominance and blood groups. Ask Grade 12 learners to solve inheritance problems and explain the difference between observed traits and allele combinations.
tasks.gr12-pedigrees-sex-linkage-mutations-t2: Topic: Pedigrees, Sex Linkage and Mutations. Cover pedigree symbols, patterns of inheritance through generations, sex-linked traits such as haemophilia and colour blindness, carriers, and how mutations create genetic variation. Ask Grade 12 learners to interpret pedigrees, predict offspring outcomes for sex-linked traits and distinguish inherited mutations from acquired changes.
tasks.gr12-nervous-system-sense-organs-t2: Topic: Responding to the Environment in Humans — Nervous System and Sense Organs. Cover neurons, the central and peripheral nervous systems, reflex arcs, receptors, the structure and function of the human eye and ear, and how nerve impulses coordinate responses. Ask Grade 12 learners to label diagrams, trace pathways and explain stimulus-response mechanisms.
tasks.gr12-endocrine-homeostasis-plant-respons: Topic: Endocrine System, Homeostasis and Plant Responses. Cover endocrine glands, hormones, differences between nervous and endocrine control, negative feedback, blood glucose regulation, thermoregulation, water balance, plant hormones and tropisms. Ask Grade 12 learners to explain homeostatic control systems and interpret plant-response experiments.
tasks.gr12-genetic-engineering-t2: Topic: Genetic Engineering (Grade 12, Term 2). Cover genetic engineering and biotechnology, recombinant DNA (restriction enzymes cut, DNA ligase joins, plasmids carry the gene into bacteria, human insulin made by bacteria), genetically modified organisms (Bt maize and cotton from Bacillus thuringiensis, golden rice and beta-carotene, benefits and concerns such as gene flow to wild relatives), stem cells (unspecialised, embryonic vs adult, bone marrow transplants for leukaemia, ethical views) and cloning (plant cuttings and tissue culture, Dolly the sheep by nuclear transfer without fertilisation, same DNA). State ethical issues as views people hold. Do not ask for dates or numbers that CAPS does not give. Ask Grade 12 learners to define, identify, explain and compare.
tasks.gr12-dna-fingerprinting-t2: Topic: DNA Fingerprinting, Paternity Testing and Mitochondrial DNA (Grade 12, Term 2). Cover a DNA profile as a pattern of bands made by gel electrophoresis (biggest fragments nearest the wells), paternity testing (the child's bands that the mother does not have must come from the father; a man who lacks one is excluded), forensic matching of a scene sample to suspects (an identical pattern is a match; a match shows the DNA could be the suspect's, not proof of guilt), and mitochondrial DNA (inherited from the mother only, changes only by mutation, used to trace maternal lineages and the African origin of modern humans). Describe band positions as numbers (1 is nearest the wells) because there is no picture. Ask Grade 12 learners to read profiles and reason, and to explain why.
tasks.gr12-nervous-disorders-injuries-drugs-t2: Topic: Nervous system: disorders, injuries and the effects of drugs (Grade 12 Life Sciences, Term 2). Cover Alzheimer's disease and multiple sclerosis, brain and spinal injuries and stem cell research, the effects of dagga, heroin, ecstasy and tik on the nervous system (effects and harms only, no use or dosing details), and the reaction-time investigation (mean, speed in m/s, distance travelled in the reaction time). Help: trusted adult, clinic, school counsellor, Childline 116 for under-18s. Give all data in the question.
